subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled producer that asks for bad paths, change the generic read tool's directory behavior, or fold this issue into the broad Gateway RSS tracker after preserving its unique logs?
rationale: Current source proves only partial fixes; the remaining CORE.md and directory-read behavior requires maintainer intent because a generic read-tool semantic change could affect existing agent/tool contracts, while the RSS claim still needs live proof.

options.title: Reproduce Producer First
options.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-release scheduler/Gateway RSS proof, and repair the specific producer or prompt path that emits bad reads.

options.title: Change Read Tool Contract
options.body: Make read handle directories as listings, accepting a broader model-facing tool behavior change that needs explicit owner approval and tests.

options.title: Fold Into RSS Tracker
options.body: Preserve this issue's logs on the broad Gateway memory tracker if maintainers decide the file-read errors are only symptoms rather than a distinct fix boundary.

recommendation.title: Reproduce Producer First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, collect current-release scheduler/Gateway RSS proof, and repair the specific producer or prompt path that emits bad reads.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history in both the read-tool and heartbeat scheduler surfaces where the producer-versus-tool boundary needs to be chosen.
